title: Restriction along a locally cofibrant dg quasi-equivalence
statement:
Use the projective enriched diagram model structures of [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]. Let $\mathcal N$ satisfy that node's hypotheses: it is a complete and cocomplete locally presentable complex-enriched, tensored and cotensored cofibrantly generated model category satisfying the enriched model axiom, with a generating set of cofibrations whose domains and codomains are cofibrant. Let $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ be a quasi-equivalence of small dg categories over $\mathbf Z$ [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure]. Assume every morphism complex of both $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal E$ is cofibrant in the projective model structure on complexes. Precomposition $f^*:\mathcal N^{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal N^{\mathcal C}$ has an enriched left adjoint $f_!$ (enriched left Kan extension). This adjunction is a Quillen equivalence: $f_!$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, and its derived adjunction on localizations at objectwise weak equivalences is an equivalence of categories. Since $f^*$ already preserves every objectwise weak equivalence, the right side of this derived adjunction is induced directly by precomposition. Write $W_{\mathcal E}$ and $W_{\mathcal C}$ for the objectwise weak equivalences in the two diagram categories. In particular
$$f^*: \mathcal N^{\mathcal E}[W_{\mathcal E}^{-1}]\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal N^{\mathcal C}[W_{\mathcal C}^{-1}]$$
is an equivalence of ordinary localized categories. No local cofibrancy or flatness is required of an additional dg category used to present $\mathcal N$ as a module category.

external.document: Bertrand Toën, The homotopy theory of dg-categories and derived Morita theory, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337
external.place: Section 3, Proposition 3.2, hypothesis (2), and its proof; read online, not archived in literature/.

proof.text:
Put $L=f_!$ and $R=f^*$. The projective structures and the free-diagram/evaluation adjunctions exist by [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]. Construct $LF$ at $e\in\mathcal E$ by the coequalizer
$$\coprod_{c,c'}\mathcal E(fc',e)\otimes\mathcal C(c,c')\otimes F(c)\rightrightarrows\coprod_c\mathcal E(fc,e)\otimes F(c).$$
One arrow composes in $\mathcal E$ after applying $f$; the other uses the action of $\mathcal C$ on $F$. Composition in $\mathcal E$ gives its dg-diagram action. A map out of the coequalizer is precisely a family compatible with these two actions, so the tensor adjunction identifies its complex of maps into a diagram $G$ with the complex of maps $F\to RG$. This constructs the enriched adjunction. All sums are small because $\mathcal C$ is small. The colimits used here, and all colimits of enriched diagrams, are computed objectwise: tensoring by any complex is a left adjoint, so it commutes with colimits and extends each action to the objectwise colimit, with its identities checked on the colimit injections. Precomposition therefore preserves all colimits, as well as all objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations. Transposing a lifting square shows that $L$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Thus $L\dashv R$ is a Quillen adjunction.

proof.text: For a cofibrant $P\in\mathcal N$, the tensor adjunction $-\otimes P:\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,-)$ is Quillen. Indeed, put $0\to P$ into the enriched model axiom of [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]; its displayed map reduces to $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,X)\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,Y)$ for a (trivial) fibration $X\to Y$, because $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(0,-)=0$. The projective model structure on complexes is [lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model], at $R=\mathbf Z$. The weak-equivalence preservation clause of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] now shows that $K\otimes P\to K'\otimes P$ is a weak equivalence whenever $K\to K'$ is a quasi-isomorphism between cofibrant complexes. This uses cofibrancy of both complexes, not preservation of all quasi-isomorphisms by tensoring.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison: homotopical tensor on cofibrant complexes; agent expansion of Toën, Proposition 3.2(2), read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, pp. 12–13.

proof.text:
Write $h_cP=\mathcal C(c,-)\otimes P$ and $h_{fc}P=\mathcal E(fc,-)\otimes P$. For cofibrant $P$, these diagrams are cofibrant by the free-diagram/evaluation adjunction of [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]: evaluation preserves trivial fibrations. The two adjunctions identify $L(h_cP)$ with $h_{fc}P$, since maps from either into $G$ are maps $P\to G(fc)$. Under this identification the unit $\eta_{h_cP}$ at $c'$ is
$$\mathcal C(c,c')\otimes P\xrightarrow{f_{c,c'}\otimes1}\mathcal E(fc,fc')\otimes P.$$
The map $f_{c,c'}$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the quasi-equivalence definition in [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], and its two complexes are cofibrant by the assumption that every morphism complex of $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal E$ is cofibrant. Step 2 therefore makes this unit an objectwise weak equivalence.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison: unit calculation on free diagrams; agent expansion of Toën, Proposition 3.2(2), read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, pp. 12–13.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the specified set of generating cofibrations of $\mathcal N$. By [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model], $I_{\mathcal C}=\{h_c i:c\in\mathcal C,\ i\in I\}$ generates the projective cofibrations, its domains and codomains are cofibrant, and $\mathcal N^{\mathcal C}$ is locally presentable. Apply [lem-coef-presentable-cellular-factorization] to the initial map $0\to F$ of a cofibrant diagram. It gives $0\to Z\xrightarrow{p}F$, where $Z$ has a small continuous filtration starting from $0$, with successor stages pushouts of coproducts of $I_{\mathcal C}$, and $p$ has the right lifting property against $I_{\mathcal C}$. The generator characterization makes $p$ a trivial fibration. Cofibrancy of $F$ supplies a section $s:F\to Z$ with $ps=1_F$, by lifting $0\to F$ against $p$. Thus $F$ is a retract of $Z$. Every stage is cofibrant: a lift against a coproduct of generating cofibrations is obtained by taking the lift on each summand; a lift against its pushout is the same lifting problem by the pushout universal property. Compositions of left lifting maps remain in the class, and at a limit the compatible lifts extend uniquely along the defining colimit. This last statement follows by choosing the lift successively, starting at $0$, and using the colimit cocone at each limit.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison: cellular filtration and retract of a cofibrant diagram; agent expansion of Toën, Proposition 3.2(2), read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, pp. 12–13.

proof.text: For each $c'\in\mathcal C$, compare the two colimit-preserving functors $A(F)=F(c')$ and $B(F)=(LF)(fc')$ from $\mathcal N^{\mathcal C}$ to $\mathcal N$, with natural transformation $\eta(F)(c'):A(F)\to B(F)$. Both send cofibrant objects to cofibrant objects and cofibrations to cofibrations: for $A$ use local cofibrancy of $\mathcal C$ and evaluation in [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]; for $B$ use the Quillen property of $L$ and local cofibrancy of $\mathcal E$ before evaluation at $fc'$. Prove that $\eta(Z_\alpha)(c')$ is a weak equivalence by transfinite induction on the filtration of step 4. At $0$ both values are initial and the unit is the identity. At a successor stage, the coproducts of units on attaching domains and codomains are weak equivalences by step 3 and clause (a) of [lem-coef-model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison]. Apply clause (b) to the map between the two evaluated attaching pushout squares: the attaching leg is a cofibration in each square, all three input objects in each span are cofibrant, and the third comparison is the inductive hypothesis. At a nonzero limit stage use clause (c): both evaluated chains are continuous, start cofibrantly, and have cofibration successor maps. This proves the induction, including a limit final stage. Naturality of $\eta$ makes $\eta_F(c')$ a retract of $\eta_Z(c')$ via $s,p$ from step 4, so it too is a weak equivalence. As $c'$ is arbitrary, the unit $F\to RLF$ is an objectwise weak equivalence for every cofibrant $F$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison: successor, limit and retract steps for the unit; agent expansion of Toën, Proposition 3.2(2), read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, pp. 12–13.

proof.text: For every cofibrant $X\in\mathcal N$, [lem-coef-chain-interval-tensor-cylinder] supplies the chain-interval good cylinder $X\amalg X\to J\otimes X\to X$, without requiring $X$ fibrant. By [lem-coef-enriched-homotopy-localization], degree-minus-one enriched homotopies with cofibrant source identify the two maps in the ordinary localization. In particular closed degree-zero maps with enriched homotopy inverses between cofibrant objects become isomorphisms there. These two general facts replace the inline cylinder and enriched-homotopy arguments of the returned step.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison: essential surjectivity, explicit chain-interval homotopy, and detection of weak equivalences; agent expansion of Toën, Proposition 3.2(2), read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, pp. 12–13.

proof.text: Now let $u:G\to H$ be a map of $\mathcal E$-diagrams with $Ru$ an objectwise weak equivalence. Choose functorial projective cofibrant replacements $QG\to G$, $QH\to H$ and their induced map $Qu$, using [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model]. Their values are cofibrant in $\mathcal N$ because $\mathcal E$ is locally cofibrant. The natural replacement squares and two-out-of-three imply that $(Qu)(fc)$ is a weak equivalence for every $c$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison: essential surjectivity, explicit chain-interval homotopy, and detection of weak equivalences; agent expansion of Toën, Proposition 3.2(2), read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, pp. 12–13.

proof.text: For $e\in\mathcal E$, essential surjectivity in [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure] gives $c$ and closed degree-zero arrows $a:fc\to e$, $b:e\to fc$ representing inverse morphisms in $H^0\mathcal E$. Thus $ba-1$ and $ab-1$ are boundaries of degree-$-1$ morphisms. The strict dg diagrams $QG,QH$ carry these equalities to enriched homotopies between their composites and identities. By step 6, their maps along $a$ are isomorphisms in the ordinary localization of $\mathcal N$. Write $\gamma:\mathcal N\to\mathcal N[W^{-1}]$ for ordinary localization. Naturality along $a$ gives the explicit equality $\gamma((Qu)(e))=\gamma(QH(a))\circ\gamma((Qu)(fc))\circ\gamma(QG(a))^{-1}$. Each factor on the right is an isomorphism, so the left side is an isomorphism. By [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences], $(Qu)(e)$ is a weak equivalence. The replacement square and two-out-of-three then imply the same for $u(e)$. This holds for every $e$. The argument uses cofibrant replacements of strict diagrams, not enriched replacement functors on $\mathcal N$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, middle finite mapping-complex comparison: essential surjectivity, explicit chain-interval homotopy, and detection of weak equivalences; agent expansion of Toën, Proposition 3.2(2), read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408337, pp. 12–13.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] to $L\dashv R$ from step 1 and pass to the ordinary homotopy categories of its enhanced localizations. Since $R$ preserves every objectwise weak equivalence, its derived functor is directly induced by $R$. Choose a functorial fibrant replacement $V\to TV$ in $\mathcal N^{\mathcal E}$. For cofibrant $F$, the derived unit is represented by $F\xrightarrow{\eta_F}RLF\to R(TLF)$; the first arrow is a weak equivalence by step 5 and the second by preservation of weak equivalences by $R$. Hence the derived unit is an isomorphism on all objects after cofibrant replacement. For a fibrant $G$ on the $\mathcal E$ side, choose a cofibrant replacement $q:QRG\to RG$. The derived counit is represented by the adjoint $a:LQRG\to G$ of $q$. The ordinary adjunction identity gives
$$R(a)\circ\eta_{QRG}=q.$$
Both $q$ and $\eta_{QRG}$ are weak equivalences, the latter by step 5; two-out-of-three gives that $R(a)$ is one. Steps 7–8 then make $a$ an objectwise weak equivalence. Fibrant replacements cover every object, so the derived counit is also an isomorphism everywhere. These natural unit and counit isomorphisms exhibit the derived functors as inverse equivalences, proving the asserted Quillen equivalence and the displayed equivalence induced by $f^*$. Throughout, only the stated axioms on $\mathcal N$ and local cofibrancy of $\mathcal C,\mathcal E$ were used; any additional dg category presenting $\mathcal N$ as a module category is untouched.
